name: /pattern-review
description: Analyze recurring themes, repeated context, and friction patterns across recent sessions — surfaces what should become skills, PROJECT_MEMORY entries, or code improvements

steps.action: Query RAG memory for conversation patterns and friction signals from recent events
steps.context:
Search memory for recurring topics and friction patterns across the past 30 days.

Run these searches using the RAG memory tool (mcp_enkratflow-me_query_memory):
  1. query='conversation patterns friction recurring topics' project='{current_project}' limit=10
  2. query='candidate skill PROJECT_MEMORY repeated question' project='{current_project}' limit=10
  3. query='what was re-explained context gap' project='{current_project}' limit=10

Also check local event files for ## Conversation patterns sections:
  grep -r 'Recurring\|Friction\|Candidate skill\|Candidate PROJECT_MEMORY\|Context gap' .exocortex/events/ 2>/dev/null | sort | head -50

Then compile a PATTERN REPORT:

=== PATTERN REPORT — {YYYY-MM-DD} ===

## Hot topics (appeared 2+ times)
(List topics that recur across events and sessions — these are re-explanation tax)
- [topic]: appeared [N] times — [brief description of what keeps getting re-explained]

## Friction hotspots (things that took too long)
- [friction point]: [what made it slow/hard]

## Skill candidates (repeating how-to patterns)
- [skill name]: [what it would cover and why it keeps coming up]

## PROJECT_MEMORY candidates (gotchas that keep appearing)
- [entry]: [the permanent fact that should be documented so no AI ever rediscovers it]

## Context gaps (things not written down anywhere)
- [gap]: [what a future agent would need to know]

## Recommended actions
1. [Most impactful action — e.g. create skill X]
2. [Second action]
3. [Third action]

If there are no ## Conversation patterns sections in events yet (this is the first run), note that and instead analyze the session summaries for recurring themes.

Present the full report to the user.

steps.prompt: Pattern report ready. What would you like to act on?

options.label: Create skill from top candidate
options.action: Draft a new SKILL.md for the top skill candidate and save it to .exocortex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md — use the existing skill format

options.label: Add entries to PROJECT_MEMORY
options.action: Append all PROJECT_MEMORY candidates to .exocortex/PROJECT_MEMORY.md in the appropriate section — use SPECIFIC wording so future AI never rediscovers these gotchas

options.label: Capture all as interrupts
options.action: Call mcp_enkratflow-me_capture_interrupt for each candidate (skill, memory, code fix) so they queue for /groom processing

options.label: Full action — do all three
options.action: Create skill, update PROJECT_MEMORY, AND capture remaining items as interrupts — do all in sequence

options.label: Just show the report — no action yet
options.action: Acknowledge and hold — user will decide later

steps.action: Execute chosen action, confirm what was created/updated, and note when to run /pattern-review again
steps.context:
Execute the chosen action from the previous step. Be specific about what was written and where.

After completing, remind the user:
'Tip: /pattern-review gets more powerful as ## Conversation patterns sections accumulate in events. Run it monthly or after any sprint where you noticed heavy context re-explanation. Each run should reduce the re-explanation tax for the next month.'
